label: copy phase: fed-back "2" or "t" early in the copy (recall_idx 2-3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original inputs or <DEL>), and only when the input token is the digit 2 (75% of mass) or the letter t (25%). Almost all of it is at recall_idx 2-3 (94% of mass), i.e. when orig(1) or orig(2) is 2/t and is being fed back in; recall_idx 1 and 4+ are weak or silent. It is strongest when the next token to output is also 2 or t (e.g. original prefix ? 2 t ...; top example z 2 t 3 ... activates on the fed-back 2), and it is larger for longer sequences (more outputs still to go, to_go 3-6). The trigger set is necessary but far from sufficient: only ~7% of 2/t inputs at recall_idx 2-3 activate. Adding out_tok in {2,t} raises dev precision to 0.46 but drops mass recall to 0.53, so the remaining gating (out_tok, L/to_go, context) is graded and not captured by a simple rule. Does not fire on any other input token (k/w/o etc. have only a handful of activations).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 2, t, k, -, w, o; least: m, q, <DEL>, v) and the token being output (most: t, 2, k, p, 3, o; least: b, f, h, 0); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, recall_idx=3, t=10.
